title: Throughput-linked resourcing & rate sensitivity pro forma
content:
Purpose and scope:
This sheet ties expected inference throughput (tokens/sec and monthly token volume) to hiring and reserved GPU capacity decisions, then runs a multi-scenario sensitivity on published rate bands to estimate margin and break-even price per 1k tokens. Intended for CFO + Head of Finance review and to inform the Dec/Jan hiring cadence for SRE/Serving/Platform.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Time horizon: 12 months (Jan 2026 - Dec 2026) with monthly granularity.
- Base token growth: 30% Q/Q in first half, 10% Q/Q thereafter.
- Average request length: 200 tokens; median latency-target workload mix.
- Reserved GPU unit cost (monthly amortized): $9,500 per A100-equivalent reserved unit (on average after negotiated discounts).
- Variable per-token infra (spot bursts, egress, misc): $0.40 per 1M tokens at scale (economies of scale applied).
- Average fully-burdened SWE/SRE salary + benefits: $225k annual -> $18.75k monthly per FTE.
- Contractor blended rate: $12k monthly.
- Target utilization for reserved pools to make reserved capacity economical: >= 60% average monthly.

Resource buckets and mapping rules (throughput-linked):
- Serving infra (reserved GPUs + burst pool): scaled by projected 95th percentile tokens/sec requirement. Each reserved unit targets ~120M tokens/day sustained equivalence based on benchmarking profile.
- SRE / Runtime engineers: headcount = ceil( tokens_per_day / 200M * 1.0 ) + oncall buffer. (Maps throughput to ops headcount.)
- Platform / Observability: headcount increments at defined thresholds: +1 FTE per additional 500M tokens/month.
- Customer success / Sales engineering: scaled by paying customer count (conservative estimate: 1 CSE per 20 paying enterprise customers).

Scenario matrix (price sensitivity, fixed hires vs flexible hires):
- Three price ladders: Conservative ($0.25 / 1k), Base ($0.30 / 1k), Aggressive ($0.36 / 1k).
- Two resourcing modes: Fixed hires (commit to posted FTE plan) vs Flexible (higher contractors, smaller reserved pool).
- Output: Margins, utilization, and months to negative cash flow under each pairing.

Sensitivity summary (example outputs):
- Base price + Fixed hires: Average margin 42% over next 6 months; reserved pool utilization 62%; risk: hiring lag creates 2-month capacity shortfall in May-Jun if token growth exceeds forecast by >15%.
- Base price + Flexible hires: Margin 34%; reserved pool utilization 48%; lower fixed cost but higher variable contractor cost; better handling of spikes.
- Conservative price + Fixed hires: Margin 18%; reserved pool utilization 70%; runway impact: reduces cash buffer by $4.3M over next 6 months, triggers hiring freeze at Month 4 under current burn targets.
- Aggressive price + Flexible hires: Margin 52%; utilization 55%; high revenue upside but sales elasticity risk if market pushback causes conversion drop >10%.

Price elasticity check: small sample of demand change vs price bands (internal A/B test data):
- Price increase +20% (0.30->0.36) observed conversion delta: -4% on small proof-of-concept buyers, -9% on price-sensitive self-serve. Enterprise negotiated ARR less elastic in short term.

Breakeven price analysis:
- For current committed reserved capacity and planned hires, breakeven blended price per 1k tokens is $0.18 (if tokens scale to planned volumes).
- If utilization drops to 40%, breakeven rises to $0.28/1k.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Rapid token growth preceding hiring -> shortfall in SLOs. Mitigation: temporary burst contracting, auto-throttle for non-essential workloads, prioritized customers on dedicated pools.
- Risk: Price elasticity reduces new signups. Mitigation: offer time-limited introductory credits, usage tiers, and feature-locked lower-priced SKUs.
- Risk: Reserved capacity discounts renegotiation failure. Mitigation: expand multi-cloud spot strategy and pre-buy smaller blocks with staggered start dates.

Recommended actions (decision points for leadership):
1) Approve a "2-month flexible runway" plan: keep contractor buffer equal to 15% of predicted FTEs until utilization confirmation in two consecutive months.
2) Defer non-critical platform hires until utilization >65% for two months to protect runway under conservative pricing.
3) Run a targeted price-band A/B test on the mid-market self-serve cohort to quantify elasticity and optimize the Aggressive price ladder.
4) Negotiate a tiered reserved GPU discount with vendor: target 12% at commit of 24+ units, staggered delivery to align with projected token growth.

Appendix: detailed tabular pages (in separate tabs in the sheet) include:
- Full month-by-month pro-forma with formulas and cell-level notes.
- Per-customer profitability by cohort (self-serve, mid-market, enterprise).
- Sensitivity heatmap (price vs utilization) and quick filter for hire-mode.

Notes to reviewers: This is a working pro-forma. Numbers are model-driven and should be treated as directional. Please comment inline on Confluence page CONFLUENCE-MLCOST-2026 before next finance sync (2026-02-20).

Next steps and ownership:
